newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline holds steady as swaps rumours swirl.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline holds steady as swaps rumours swirl.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices held steady at midday as talk surrounding the swaps positions of one trader continued to cloud the barge market and draw mixed opinions on its fundamental condition.
A trader familiar with that firm's gasoline positions said it did not have a leveraged position and had no interest in boosting the physical market.

Its buying in the barge market this week has been cited by other traders as a primary reason for the firmer tone in prices. Stronger IPE Brent prices and NYMEX unleaded futures in overnight ACCESS trading also helped on Friday.
"We are balanced. We are long swaps and short physical on a one-to-one relationship," this trader said.
"We do not have a leveraged position...We have no need to keep this market up."
He said Rotterdam refinery material was scarce and was the reason for his trading firm paying a premium over ARA gasoline in the last few days.
"Anyone knows there is a premium for Rotterdam refinery material," he said, adding that the refiners were not offering a significant amount of material.
Traders said the firm had paid higher than normal premiums for refinery gasoline in recent days.
Premium unleaded barges were assessed at $189/$191 fob ARA, while bids for Rotterdam refinery material were heard at $192, traders said.
Deals were heard done at $188 and $189 for fob ARA and at $191 for Amsterdam-Rotterdam.
Prices for first half July were heard near $185, in line with swaps.

A trader at a large European oil company, however, argued that the trading house was indeed trying to keep barge prices higher to capitalise on a long position in the swaps market. He said this may continue for the rest of the month, despite what he believed was a wide availability of barges.
"There is more than enough material in the ARA market available," he said. "I don't see the barges as tight...The fundamentals are not bullish anymore."

He said refiners in ARA were running flat out and compounding the growing supply pool from a closed arbitrage to the States. He also anticipated higher exports out of the UK after the government's budget on July 2.

The spread between premium unleaded and regular unleaded should also widen due to unsold regular unleaded cargoes and the closed arb, he said. He put the spread close to $7-$8 and said it could weaken toward $10.
